subject: Finlytics DPA: redlines, routing, and signature plan

Subject: Redwood DPA - initial redlines

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal has attached a set of commercial and privacy redlines to your standard DPA. Key asks from our side:

- Retainability: 3 year data retention requirement for customer event logs (we propose exception handling).
- Subprocessor list: request for quarterly notice and 30-day objection window.
- Liability cap: customer is asking for a limited carve-out for data breach fines (they flagged GDPR regulator fines).

See attached: Finlytics_DPA_redline_20261218.docx (redline). We need a managed signature workflow — they prefer DocuSign. Can you confirm the signatory and timeline? Procurement is targeting a Jan 5 go-live.

Marissa / Karthik / Laura —

Forwarding Finlytics' redlines. They have a few asks that touch legal ops and privacy. High level: quarterly subprocessor notice (30d objection), a request on retention for event logs, and a ask to revisit the liability cap carve-out for regulatory fines.

Can legal ops / privacy please:
- Confirm which of these we can accept as-is, which need counter-proposals, and the least-risk language for retention and subprocessors.
- Recommend a signatory and whether we should use DocuSign routing to include both procurement and legal on the customer side.
- Prepare a short redline summary I can share back with Jason by EOD Monday (20th).

They attached the redline doc (attached here). I'll own commercial negotiation and coordinating procurement logistics.

Thanks — appreciate quick thoughts.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood DPA - initial redlines

Thanks for the ping, Vanessa. I reviewed the redlines and drafted a short reply and a proposed set of counter-language. Summary below (and I uploaded a working spreadsheet "Redline_Summary_Finlytics_20261219.xlsx" to Drive).

Summary of position:
- Subprocessor quarterly notice: Accept with modification — agree to quarterly disclosures but limit objection window to 15 days for operational practicality; propose a standing exception process for time-sensitive infra changes.
- Retention for event logs: Offer a compromise — preserve 12-month default plus add a contractual option for up to 36 months when requested in writing with documented business need and customer-provided justification.
- Liability/Regulatory fines: Push back on unlimited carve-outs for fines. Propose language that allows indemnity for direct regulatory fines only where Redwood is adjudicated liable and had a gross negligence determination; cap at statutory penalty amounts where possible.

Routing/signature: Recommend the following execution flow:
1) Final redline agreed via email (legal ops + customer legal).
2) Redwood legal to prepare final DPA PDF for signature.
3) DocuSign envelope to be routed to Finlytics' authorized signatory (Procurement) and our authorized signatory (CRO or authorized delegate).

Action items for Monday 20th:
- Karthik: finalize negotiated text and confirm whether 15-day window is feasible from an ops standpoint.
- Laura: confirm that the 36-month retention carve-out is acceptable from a privacy/program perspective and whether we need a DPIA note.
- Vanessa: propose a signing date to customer (I suggest Dec 30 or Jan 4 depending on internal approvals).

I'll be on email over the weekend if you need quick edits.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment referenced: Redline_Summary_Finlytics_20261219.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood DPA - initial redlines

Quick update from legal ops and infra:

- Subprocessor notice: 15-day objection window is acceptable. Ops recommends we add a clause that allows emergency deployment notifications that are effective immediately but will be memorialized in the quarterly report.
- Retention: 12-month default + contractual extension up to 36 months is operationally fine provided customer signs an addendum specifying business justification. We'll track via our retention ledger.
- DPIA: Laura, please confirm if a lightweight DPIA is needed for the 36-month scenario; if so, we should include a provision that customer may request a DPIA and Redwood will cooperate.

I've attached a short negotiated text excerpt in the HubSpot comment and updated the Drive doc. I also flagged the liability paragraph: we should offer the regulatory-fines carve-out with explicit gross negligence requirement — reduces litigation exposure.

I can prepare the final DPA PDF by EOD Tuesday and put it into DocuSign envelope. Who should be the Redwood signatory? I recommend CRO (Mark Roberts) or, if timing is tight, our Head of Finance (Priya Natarajan).

— Karthik Iyer
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Related link: https://hubspot.company/notes/DL-98271-ops

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jason Cole <jason.cole@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA - redlines, routing, and signature plan

Jason —

Thanks for the redlines and for the quick turnaround from your side. Confirming Redwood's proposed compromise below (summary for sign-off):

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide quarterly subprocessor disclosures. We propose a 15-day objection window (reduction from your requested 30d) with an emergency deployment carve-out that will be memorialized in the next report.
- Event log retention: Default 12 months; customers may contractually opt-in to up to 36 months with a documented business justification and an addendum.
- Liability/regulatory fines: Redwood cannot accept an uncapped carve-out. We propose indemnity only where Redwood is adjudicated grossly negligent, with remedies aligned to statutory penalty frameworks.

Next steps:
1) If Finlytics accepts the above, we will finalize a clean DPA and send via DocuSign. Karthik will prepare the envelope.
2) Proposed Redwood signatory: Priya Natarajan (Head of Finance) — will sign on behalf of Redwood. Please confirm your authorized signatory and whether Procurement or Legal should be the first signer on your side.
3) Targeted signature window: Dec 30–Jan 4. Let me know if you need earlier execution and we can escalate to Marissa to authorize.

I've attached the consolidated redline summary for your review.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Attachments: Redline_Summary_Finlytics_20261219.xlsx, Finlytics_DPA_redline_20261218.docx
